source_refs.note: Topic 18.5.2 with the Labrador, Bombay phenotype and foxglove examples (PDF 98-100); Figures 18.8 and 18.9 are replaced by the original diagram.

blocks.text: Most traits arise from interactions between different genes. In allelic interactions the alleles of the same gene interact, as in incomplete dominance, co-dominance and multiple alleles. In non-allelic interactions the alleles of different genes, at different loci, interact; a common example is epistasis.

blocks.title: Epistasis
blocks.text: Epistasis is gene interaction in which an allele masks or modifies the effect of the alleles of other genes at other loci. The allele that masks or modifies is epistatic; the allele whose effect is masked or modified is hypostatic.
The book gives the allele for baldness as epistatic to the alleles for black and blonde hair. (Baldness is described again in topic 18.8.3 as a sex-influenced trait.)

items: Gene B controls pigment colour: B gives black and b brown, so BB or Bb is black and bb brown.

Gene E controls deposition of pigment in the fur: E allows it, while e (when ee) is epistatic to B and b and blocks it, so EE or Ee dogs have pigmented fur but ee dogs are yellow whether B or b is present.

blocks.text: When two heterozygous black dogs (BbEe x BbEe) are crossed, the offspring are black, brown and yellow in a 9:3:4 ratio.

blocks.alt: Left: a 4 x 4 Punnett square for Labrador BbEe x BbEe with gametes BE, Be, bE and be; boxes are coloured black (B_E_), brown (bbE_) or yellow (any ee), giving 9 black : 3 brown : 4 yellow. Right: foxglove DdWw selfed gives 12 white (W_), 3 dark red (D_ww) and 1 light red (ddww), with a note that W confines pigment to small spots inside.
blocks.caption: Epistasis in Labrador coat colour and foxglove flower colour (original diagram after Figures 18.8 and 18.9).
blocks.long_description: In Labradors gene B decides the pigment (B black, b brown) and gene E decides whether pigment is laid down in the fur; ee blocks it, so any ee dog is yellow whatever its B alleles. BbEe x BbEe therefore gives 9 B_E_ black, 3 bbE_ brown and 3 + 1 = 4 yellow (B_ee and bbee), a 9:3:4 ratio. In foxglove D gives dark red and dd light red pigment, while a dominant W limits the pigment to small spots on the inner side so the flower looks white; DdWw selfed gives 9 + 3 = 12 white, 3 dark red and 1 light red, a 12:3:1 ratio.

blocks.text: Expression of the ABO genotypes also depends on another gene, H, which makes the H substance, the precursor of the A and B antigens; IA and IB make enzymes that convert H substance into antigen-A and antigen-B. A person with IA and IB but genotype hh makes no H substance, so no A or B antigen is made and the person has the O phenotype. This Bombay phenotype was discovered in Bombay in 1952 and is mostly found in India, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Iran.

items: Gene D: the dominant D produces dark red petals and the recessive d light red, so DD or Dd is dark red and dd light red.
Gene W, at another locus: the dominant W limits the pigment made by D or d to small spots, so the petals look white from outside; the recessive w allows uniform pigment.

blocks.text: A heterozygous DdWw plant has white flowers, because W limits the pigment to small spots on the inner side. If it is self-fertilized it gives white, dark red and light red flowers in a 12:3:1 ratio.

blocks.prompt: In BbEe x BbEe Labradors, why is the yellow class 4 out of 16 and not 3?
blocks.explanation: Every ee dog is yellow: 3 B_ee plus 1 bbee = 4. The 9:3:3:1 classes B_ee and bbee merge because ee hides B and b.

blocks.prompt: What genotype does a Bombay-phenotype person with blood group O by test, but IA IB genes, have at the H gene?
blocks.explanation: hh: no H substance is made, so the IA and IB enzymes have nothing to convert into A or B antigens.

items: Epistasis: an allele at one locus masks or modifies another locus.
Labrador BbEe x BbEe: 9 black : 3 brown : 4 yellow.
Foxglove DdWw selfed: 12 white : 3 dark red : 1 light red.
Bombay phenotype: hh gives O whatever the ABO alleles.
